Amazing game held back by garbage port. Don’t buy. The iPad and iPhone UI/UX is terrible. I bought this game day 1 and there were significant issues such as text being comically small and selecting and playing cards being super wonky and often times resulting in wrong cards being played. 

The newest update has made the game unplayable. It is frustrating, almost impossible to deselect a card once you have selected. You need to constantly select cards so you can read what they do. It’s like the devs didn’t even QA or play test the game at all on ios!

Go play gwent instead. Gwent has excellent controls.

reviews.title: My favorite rogue like
reviews.text:
I own this on PC and iOS. If I had other means of playing it, I probably would! 

There are times when I know a run is going bad, but I’ll keep going anyway because sometimes it just takes ONE more relic and boom, complete turn around and off to the top of the tower with me. 

Other times there are heartbreaking losses at the very bitter end. I feel less bad about those, now, as this game is meant to be challenging.

I just hit about 125 hours of playtime on PC. I would wager I’m at around 10 hours on iOS. I would be at more, however I’m back in school now, and I can’t afford to play this amazing game when i should be studying. 

I highly recommend. The developers are awesome. Support them if you can!

reviews.title: Great, except for the heart…
reviews.text: Overall, I quite liked this game. It’s fun and engaging but still something you don’t need to constantly pay attention to. Where it really falls down is the final boss. The heart is WAY overpowered and seeming almost impossible to beat. There’s just no reason it should be that tough. Maybe one out of ten runs even makes it that far, and the fact that you don’t even get a chance to heal before hand it absolutely insane. Terrible boss design and completely turned me off this game.

reviews.title: The worst Version of the best card game
reviews.text: As someone who has over 2000 hours into Slay the Spire on steam, I was delighted to see that it finally came to mobile, and while its not a perfect port by any means, it may still be the best bang for your buck on the entire App Store. There are bugs still, and crashes, the UI is not as polished as one may hope, but at the end of the day even being a subpar version of itself still puts this game in a league of its own.

reviews.title: NOT optimized for iPhone.
reviews.text:
I have much experience with this game prior to this iOS version, and I truly enjoy it.  It is genuinely so much fun.  My gripes are with this are purely for this version:
I got this game to play on both iPad and iPhone, and I used to play it on other platforms.  Most everything is optimized on iPad, it functions well. 1) It definitely needs 120Hz ProMotion enabled.  2) The text is entirely too small on iPhone, and many of the assets are difficult to distinguish, as well as some of them bleed off the screen.

reviews.title: Poor Update
reviews.text:
Latest update 2.2.2 feels significantly worse than before. The touch controls feel overall slower. The card hovering below the finger feature felt more natural, and is now removed. I believe I also used to be able to slide cards to an enemy as the animation was completing, sort of stacking up the moves, making the game feel faster. I think that was removed as well. The cycling between cards in your deck also feels slow.

In addition, the layout of the map went from feeling too close up, to too far away. Is there not a happy medium?

I’m curious what motivated these strange changes?

reviews.title: Excellent game, mobile version needs work.
reviews.text:
As a StS player that has nearly 700 hours on PC, I was very excited to finally have this game on mobile. For the most part, it’s a great game on mobile too. There is a glaring issues however... the UI is way too small for mobile. You are constantly mis-clicking everything and at times it can be very frustrating. 
This I feel should be an easy fix and would drastically improve the flow of the game. So much so that I would easily bump this review to 5 stars.

reviews.title: Awesome play, horrible UI
reviews.text:
The game is great! However, there's a bunch of "did they even" on the layout. 

You can't see what a card does without pulling up on it. (Which is dumb given all the real estate. Seriously,  take a quarter inch out of the "battlefield" and move the cards up). At which point you STILL can't read it because it's centered on your finger. And you can't easily put it back in your hand - pro-tip: tap over near the bottom left or bottom right. If you tap at the top, it plays it.

reviews.title: Good game, poor port
reviews.text:
I love sts. I have almost 200 hours on pc, so I bought the mobile app. It’s the same experience, save for a few problems. Firstly, the app is very unstable. In many situations the game will crash, and in the worst situations it deletes your current game progress. Aside from that, the ui could use some changing. The text is just too small, the proportions are also a little off. Occasionally cards will select themselves and it’s a nightmare to de-select them. 
10/10 game
8/10 gameplay
5/10 ui

reviews.title: Favorite iOS Game!
reviews.text: I really wish the touch UI was a little stronger. For instance, selecting cards will hide the card description off the bottom of my iPhone 11 until I “re-select” it correctly. Also the potions are hard to select from being so small. I really enjoy the game and I hope they can make some changes for a better UX in the future. Last time STS was updated was 6 months ago... This port is so close to perfect and would love to see an update! Thank you for the amazing game!

reviews.title: Day 1 review
reviews.text: It's the same exact slay the spire we all loved on desktop. And that's part of my issue lol. It's serviceable as is, but the UI is 100% ripped straight from the original. I bet this probably looks beautiful on iPad, but on iPhone the UI is too small. All I ask for is a resize lol. No reason the card selections should be this small on my phone screen. There's plenty of room to blow them up. Love love love the game, 10/10 game, game of the year forever... But until the UI is bigger for my phone its a 4/5 for me here.

reviews.title: How can card selection be this hard
reviews.text:
This game’s card selection is all over the place. I thought my touch screen was broken with this latest update. It was way too sticky before but I figured it out. Now selecting cards on the outside is super hard, since if you touch too far towards the bottom you will close the game.

I can play APM pirates in Hearthstone Battlegrounds on my phone but this game is borderline unplayable. How is this this bad.

reviews.title: Fix the App
reviews.text:
I love Slay the Spire. I own it on Xbox and PC. Decided to pick the mobile version up for the road, and it has so major problems. When trying to play a card with a full hand, it’s way too troublesome to select the correct card. Another major issue is removing a card from your deck. You must scroll through the deck using your fingers. While scrolling, it almost always selects a card you were just scrolling by. I’ve removed some of my favorite cards without any way to cancel the apps selection. 

Please fix the app.

reviews.title: Fantastic with Bug
reviews.text:
I have played this on many platforms now and it’s a great game.  Little grind, great card play, and replayability.  Slight edge to PC versions for modding ability.

On PC I was able to immediately unlock access to Keys and Act 4.  On iOS despite beating Act 3 multiple times I cannot get access to Keys and ultimately Act 4.  

Any recommendations?  I’d rate this game higher if not for that.  I played it on Steam recently for PC and almost immediately beat Act 3 with the first 3 characters and unlocked the Keys and Act 4.  I’ve had the game on iOS for years and have beat Act 3 with ALL characters a minimum of 3 times each (more for some) and no love.  

Very frustrating. This game is therefore dead to me on iOS until that can be resolved.  I’m an Apple ecosystem person so it’s a big fat bummer to not have it work on my most used platform.

reviews.title: Awesome game, fairly decent port
reviews.text:
Gameplay is good and works reasonably well even on my iPhone 6. Good sound, performance, etc. 

Couple issues that keep it from being five stars though. First and foremost is I can’t listen to other music or podcasts while I play. This is something that should be standard on all mobile games, but I can’t multitask while I play. 

Second is that the controls are slightly off from the port. When a game starts, a card is selected. I have to be very careful to select a different card or it will play the other selected card instead. It feels like they ported over mouse controls without really thinking about them too much. It’s not bad, but could be better.

Still, it’s a great game for the price and as long as you don’t expect absolute perfection, it’s pretty good.

reviews.title: Great game, while I was able to play it.
reviews.text:
I played this game for a good hour or two the day I bought it. Put it down for a bit and tried re-opening it, only for it to freeze on the intro screen and then quickly force quit from the app. I’ve tried re-downloading as well as turning on/off my phone. No success in getting the app to open again. 

Edit: This game is really good, but I continue to have several issues opening the game. It opens on occasion with no indication as to what made it work on each given time.

reviews.title: Great game, held back by frame rate
reviews.text:
On an iPad Pro, there’s no reason this should be running at anything less than 60FPS.  Fix this.  The low frame rate makes card selection and the basic UX / UI incredibly sluggish compared to running this on Steam on any decent rig from the past decade.  The ad for the game looks to have been recorded and is playing back at a higher frame rate than the game currently plays.

This is a no brainer.  If it needs to be a setting somewhere, make it so, let us choose to place a drain on our devices as required.

I just blew through the first area and I’m down to 99% on a fresh charge.

Great job on the port devs, the FPS and some low resolution assets (map mostly) that are noticeable when holding a screen much closer to a users eyes compared to gaming on a monitor are my only complaints after the first run.

reviews.title: Not as good as other versions
reviews.text:
I played a few hours of this game on the PC and loved it, but wanted a mobile version so I wasn’t tied to a desktop to play it.

When this version came out I bought it instantly and immediately recognized it just wasn’t as good.

I’m on an iPhone XS, which is by no means a small phone, but I feel the UI just isn’t well designed and can be confusing at times. It can be hard to see what cards do, and it can be difficult to figure out how to deselect a card so you don’t play it.

The biggest issue, however, is all the bugs. The sounds drops randomly and I can’t figure out what causes it. Plus, when the sound drops the games chances to crash back to the home screen goes up significantly. I was on the 3rd boss when this happened. I dealt the final blow and poof, crash to home screen. I loaded the game back up and I had to redo the boss and lost. 

This has happened multiple times. Fix it

reviews.title: Very fun but too small on phone
reviews.text: This is pretty much a straight port of the PC game.  The game itself is addictive and very fun. I like being able to just spend the time for one or two battles and set it down until later.  As a PC port, the text on the cards is too small to read on a phone.  On my iPhone XS I have to squint and hold the phone right up to my face.  The cards already zoom a tiny bit when selected.  If they grew to screen height it would be much easier to play.

reviews.title: Fix the controls
reviews.text:
The game itself is excellent. The iOS port is pretty much crap. UI is core and this app fails to deliver. You will play cards you don’t want to, even after hours of playing. There’s no developer support button to report bugs. You may not play outside audio without workarounds.

By the way, to enable outside audio, turn it on with a function that does not minimize the game. That would be the control you slide up from the bottom of your iPhone, or an external device (earphones with a play button work).

reviews.title: Awesome but needs a few user experience upgrades
reviews.text:
Love this game. I’ve been looking for a game on my iPhone I can put down and come back to where I left off. This is perfect. 
For the love of my old eyes please provide a zoom in option. The visuals and text are tiny on my phone. Secondly there’s some unintuitive interaction when trying to determine what a keyword does... there’s not a way to hover over the keyword in the shop or question mark spots without accidentally choosing that option.

reviews.title: Great game but some issues
reviews.text:
I love this game and it plays well on my phone, however there was one issue I haven’t been able to solve. 
After you unlock beta art, I’m unable to click on the “beta art” box below cards. Idk if it’s because of the way iPhone screens are set up (the bottom is where you scroll up to leave the game) or what but I am able to click on “view upgrade”. 
I wish I could see the beta art, otherwise, it’s a 5 star game

reviews.title: Port needs work
reviews.text: I’m really glad to have this amazing game on iOS, but it’s probably the weakest version. The controls are pretty frustrating, especially on the iPhone. I’m selecting the wrong cards, and having trouble enacting them. Also this game desperately needs icloud sync. iPad works better, just because your finger can’t get in the way as much. However, I don’t want to play on the iPad, because the save file doesn’t transfer from the iPhone. Probably will stick to playing on my switch, and iPhone when I’m out and desperate.

reviews.title: Love This Game!
reviews.text: I play STS on PC and am so excited for it to come to iPad. It’s a game which holds my attention and I have +100 hours on PC already, excited to get started here. The deck building is skill-based with an element of luck and you have to adapt to whichever final boss you’re facing per act. The characters each have their own skill sets and are interesting to build with. The art is great and the fights are versatile and interesting. Wonderful game which I highly recommend.

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.text:
I bought it yesterday and played for 13 hrs already. It’s really addicting and fun. It’s challenging, but not to the point where you want to give up once you figure things out.

I will say the UI can be a little frustrating when you’re in battle. I’ve had it “auto select” cards before and didn’t realize so I accidentally played it.

reviews.title: Controller wont work on it
reviews.text: I've always loved slay the spire, but when I spent my money on it for my phone, expexting my backbone controller to work with it, I was shocked that it didnt work. Thought my backbone was the problem, so thought nothing of it. Next I paired an ebox controller to my phone, and yet, still nothing was working. I tested it on other apps, and it worked fine, so why cant I use a controller for this? People complain about the controls on mobile, so thought this could fix it. Now I've wasted my hopes, money, and am disappointed. Thanks a ton

reviews.title: Can’t recommend enough
reviews.text: One of my favorite games of all time. I’ve been playing since 2019 on steam and have around 400 total hours combined from steam, iOS, and Nintendo switch. It’s a hefty price especially for an app but it’s the full fledged game that costs $25 on all other platforms so it really is a steal. The game runs great and the iOS port is nothing short of exceptional. Support indie developers!!

reviews.title: Excellent game!
reviews.text: With so many pay to win games flooding the mobile market. Games like this are a breath of fresh air. Pay once, and get a high quality game that you can play for hours and hours. This is a simple card battler mechanic. Part dungeon crawler and part rogue like. It all comes together for a wonderful game that is easy to learn and accessible to all. But still contains plenty of depth and strategy as you play more and get better.

reviews.title: Masterpiece
reviews.text: I don’t review often but this game is deserving. I own this on PC and have a couple hundred hours into it. Fantastic game. Mechanics are solid and expertly intertwine with each other. It’s a rogue-like deck building dungeon crawler. The bosses are well designed and enemy encounters are varied with engaging attack patterns. This feels like a labor of love. Which is re-enforced by no micro transactions and free updates like adding more characters to start your adventure with. Great game from great developers. A+

reviews.title: Great game, missing save transfer
reviews.text: I love this game and was instantly addicted after buying it on steam. I got to the true boss of the game and then picked up the phone game so I could continue on the go. Was extremely disappointed that save transfers are not possible. Also, I don’t know if it’s the size of my phone screen (13 mini), but the cards are hard to read and it’s so easy to play something by accident that it can be really annoying sometimes.

reviews.title: Great game, needs optimization.
reviews.text: Gameplay is great as always and I’ve sunk countless hours into the steam version of this game, but I feel like the game could use some quality of life adjustments. The main menu options could really use being bumped up in size since their is plenty of space to feel up and it can be hard to click with your fingers. It would also really help if you could allow zooming in and out on the map to help see more closely.

reviews.title: Love it so much I own it on 3 different platforms
reviews.text:
If you ask me I say this is one of the most innovative game ideas I’ve ever encountered. A rouge like card game with 4 different archetypes all with cool synergies and a variety of mechanics that guarantees a unique run every playthrough 

Please fix crashing tho :( I foolishly tried to uninstall and reinstall in attempt to resolve the issue and lost all my progress lol

reviews.title: Fantastic game, terrible controls
reviews.text:
The game is one of my favorites. I have it on all platforms. 

However the touch version needs much more attention to detail. Accidental wrong moves can happen way to easy, looking up a card in your hand is tedious, and prone to error (e.g. why aren’t the card just higher up per se on iPad). Other actions need too much confirmation. Was really looking forward to this and very disappointed that the iOS version is the most error prone and loveless version. Recommend Mac/PC first, switch second and iOS only if you don’t have other platforms to use.

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.text: I have multiple versions of Sts but I play the app version the most. Love the content and game only issues I find is a issue on my iPhone X where I can’t turn on the beta art since it brings up the swipe up short cut on IOS would be nice if that was moved up a little more maybe even to the bottom of the card instead of under the card. Wish I could see all the nice beta art. That or add a toggle in the settings for it. Besides that great port.

reviews.title: Horrible UI
reviews.text: Imagine playing for an hour to just lose because the user interface is so bad that it doesn’t play the card you chose, for starters you can’t even see the whole text on the card if it is on the edges, then when trying to choose a card while scrolling you could accidentally tab the edge of a card and then you instantly pick it up, and lastly if press a card to read the text and then press it again or even press another card sometimes it just plays the card. Good game but horrible UI. What a shame.

reviews.title: Amazing game, needs work
reviews.text: I love Slay. Spent many many hours on PC version. Very glad there is a mobile version but it could use some optimizing. The buttons, while great size for a mouse click, are very small for a finger tap on iOS. Additionally, dragging cards up and around sometimes results in frames dropping. I’d love to be able to import my save from Steam, but in absence of that Cloud save would be nice. I can’t wait to see future versions of this port that are cleaned up a bit!

reviews.title: Almost perfect
reviews.text: I love this game, plenty of hours on other devices and I’m pumped to finally see it on mobile. There’s a major problem though with the lack of save states. I’ve lost progress mid game because I needed to do something else on my phone and I come back to see that my run restarted. There needs to be an option to save and exit midway through a game, just like the binding of Isaac or dead cells or civ 6. If that got changed this would easily be a 5 star game.

reviews.title: Epic game
reviews.text: Well I’ve played for quite a lot while on mobile it’s a great game would have given 5 stars if not for the update that zooms everything in while it’s is nice it’s pretty buggy now a lot of the text and stuff don’t line up and it feels as if it came out of nowhere if they we’re gonna make a update that impacts the look of everything is to do a full job of it or not at all.

reviews.title: I love sts!
reviews.text: Awesome game, honestly the best game I’ve played on mobile. If you’re a fan of rougelikes, then slay the spire is a must play. I will also say I’ve played this game on all platforms (mobile/console/pc) and it plays great on all of them! I’d like to see controller support for mobile, but that’s the only gripe I have. For the price it’s one of the best in the genre if not the best, definitely recommend

reviews.title: Please reduce size/frequency/visibility of “Syncing data…” text
reviews.text: Love the game have played it for 170 hours, but please change something about the newly added syncing text. It’s very distracting and annoying, and fades in and out making it even more eye grabbing. I turn off the internet whenever I play now because the syncing message is too bothersome.

reviews.title: Great game, poor optimization
reviews.text:
As a huge fan of this game, who have played over 200 hours on PC, I cannot believe how poorly optimized this game is, compared to how great the game is. 

1. UI: I am 100% sure that the developer have never tested the game on iPhone X or 11, because every time I try to drag and use a card, all I see is home screen of my iPhone. Cards are way too small, hard to choose the card I intended to choose, and even worse, it’s even more difficult to deselect the card you have chosen. 

2. Frame drop: I was never a picky gamer, especially in light of a frame drop. However, this game’s frame drop is as awful as playing the Witcher 3 on Nintendo Switch, and my eyes actually hurt because of it. Fyi, I am playin on iPhone11.

Still, this game is fun, for sure, but I would  recommend you to play it literally on ANY other platform, rather than on iOS.

reviews.title: So Fun!
reviews.text:
This game is challenging, but not in a frustrating way. It’s a rogue-like, so you have to have the mindset going in that you will fail lol. It’s more of a “How far can I get this time?” sort of game. 

The card selection from your hand each round can be fiddly. Hopefully that’s improved in a future update. A lot of reviews mention crashes, but no problems for me using 6th generation iPad running current OS (13.5.1).

reviews.title: Great Game, Poor Execution
reviews.text: I’ve been waiting for this game to come out on iOS for a while now, so I was stoked to see that it finally dropped. Upon downloading it and playing a few runs, I quickly realized that the controls were a little awkward for newer devices. That is, I found myself frequently hitting the home bar on my iPhone 11 Pro Max while trying to read what cards do. The buttons are kind of small on iPhone, and there is no cloud save, so my progress on my phone does not sync with my iPad Pro.

reviews.title: Fun but too imbalanced
reviews.text:
I keep trying to progress but the enemies become too powerful for the cards you’re given. Pretty frustrating to spend time going to the end of the second stage only to have no chance whatsoever of beating that boss. Things like starting with all defense cards while the boss is vulnerable to attack, then getting no block cards when they do their most powerful attack. I like a challenge, but imbalance like this is a pretty big flaw.

And yes, the card selection mechanism in combat is pretty bad.

reviews.title: Great game! Some minor issues though
reviews.text: This is my favorite game, so I was glad to see it on mobile. However, there are some tiny bugs and few issues (the first card you click each turn doesn’t register, the map button, deck button, and settings are all VERY close) but for the most part, great game.

reviews.title: Great game, doesn’t keep up with updates it gets on PC
reviews.text: I love the game. I play it on both PC and on my iPhone and the experience is nearly the same with the exception of a couple quirks the mobile version has. The big problem I have with the mobile version is that it doesn’t keep up with updates. There was a balance update for Slay the Spire on pc two or so months ago as this version still doesn’t have those.

reviews.title: PLEASE fix the crashing
reviews.text: I absolutely adore this game. Played it for hours and hours on PC and was refreshing daily on the App Store waiting for it to finally arrive on iOS. While not perfect, they’ve done a pretty decent job of porting it over. But I’ve gone from decent performance to crashes after nearly every match using the Assassin character. Twice now I’ve fought through an entire floor just to get to the boss and it crashes every time I beat the boss and it starts me back at the beginning of the fight

reviews.title: Great Game but suffers from ui/control issues
reviews.text:
I would have given this game a 5 star rating, but the ui is clunky and consistently erratic. 

Many cardgames on mobile feel smooth and accurate e.g. Hearthstone, Marvel Snap, balatro etc. but this game’s responsiveness is frustrating and blocks me from actually enjoying the game. 

Many times, i can’t read cards or cycle through them. Many times cards play on their own and ruin runs. 

Hopefully this is addressed in StS2 but for now and for how long this game has been out, there’s been plenty of time to fix this very obvious issue. I don’t understand a team working on this, playing and and thinking “yup, this is fine”

It’s a great game, but these mobile controls just make me close the game and do something else.

reviews.title: Bought it because they deserve it
reviews.text:
I picked this game up for free on PS+. After playing for 30+ hours I felt guilty for enjoying something this much without giving the developers money for it. 

Side bonus of having it on mobile! Worth every penny.

Thanks for making a great game. I hope you didn’t lose too much $ with it being free on PSN

reviews.title: A good port of a great game
reviews.text: Slay the Spire is one of my favorite rogue-lite style games on PC and this is a stable port, however it seems as if animations are locked at ~60 fps (maybe less?) even on the iPhone 13 Pro. Since the PC version has native support for 120 and 240 hertz refresh rates, it would be great to see the app updated with the latest version of the API to support 120 frames per second. With that added it would easily be a 5* port for me.

reviews.title: Love the game
reviews.text: I would give it a 5 out of 5 but I did already buy this game on steam which is disappointing that I had to pay twice but I love this game so much there’s a lot of strategy in what decks you pick for each character, the only thing I don’t like about the mobile version is that sometimes you accidentally swipe up when trying to play a card

reviews.title: Superb Game; UI needs tweaks
reviews.text: I’m with most other reviewers - great game but it can be hard to read text on small iPhone screens. Tapping a card makes it bigger, to facilitate reading, but in many cases not big enough - and sometimes ½ of the card stays hidden below the screen. Tweak the UI to fix this and this game will be near perfect.  As it is now - buy it anyway!  It’s a full port of the PC game and well worth the $$.

reviews.title: Great game with some ux issues
reviews.text:
I have been really enjoying this game. It's perfect for playing on the iPad. However, the experience of playing cards can be frustrating. 

Some issues I had while playing:
- I can't see the stats for all the cards at once, so I have to tap a card one at a time, to see the stats. 
- When viewing the cards, sometimes they get played, which is not always what I want to do.

reviews.title: Great game, eh adaption
reviews.text: I love this game, however my main complaint with this on IOS is that everything is too small and it’s hard to press what you want at times. If the cards were larger and easier to press that would be a great adjustment. I have yet to experience any crashes or technical issues which is great. I think minor adjustments like the card sizes and options would be a better adaption to gameplay on smaller screens.

reviews.title: Buy it
reviews.text: It’s a complete game, what more can you ask for? Yes some devices don’t always work flawlessly at first. But it’s a good game and no run thru is ever the same. Cell service or wifi are not required to play. No ads. I’ve got probably 200+ hours into it. Purchase once and play on any of your apple devices.

reviews.title: Great game, not the best version
reviews.text: I am a huge fan of Slay the Spire on PC and have been waiting for the iOS release. I am pretty disappointed with this version so far. Of the 3 runs that I have played, it has crashed over 5 times. I have also played the wrong cards because of the touch controls. I’m sure I will get used to them but it’s not as smooth as I would have hoped. Giving the app 3 stars because Slay the Spire is amazing, but wondering if I should have opted for the Switch version for mobile play.

reviews.title: Bought it again
reviews.text: I play this game on PC, and bought it again to support the devs further. This game is incredibly engaging. You'll die over and over and over again, but always be ready to pick it back up and start over because you were *so close* last time. This time you'll beat it! You'll say the Spire! And then want to do it again.

reviews.title: Game is 5/5; port is 3.5/5
reviews.text: Best deck-builder video game. I own it on multiple platforms including Nintendo switch and pc. This iOS port is manageable, but misclicks are too frequent due to the invisible cursor that is used for the port. I would suggest a control overhaul, but I understand that is an insane amount of work that would be added to the devs plate. Still my favorite mobile game, so would 100% recommend to deck-builder enthusiasts.

reviews.title: Best game on IOS... Period.
reviews.text: There's a good number of solid ports of great PC games on here, but this game more than any of them feels like a natural fit for mobile devices. The controls translate pretty seamlessly to a touch screen and the game is built for short playthroughs/extremely high replayability. The game itself is a modern classic and is well worth the asking price.

reviews.title: Game is awesome, port has iffy UX
reviews.text: I think everyone knows that this game is amazing by this point, I don’t need to go into that. But this mobile port is just ok - I’ve put many hours into it so it’s definitely still fun, but it was not optimized for touch controls. Very easy to misclick, buttons/icons are really small, controls aren’t intuitive. Would love a rehaul of the touch controls.

reviews.title: Finally.
reviews.text:
It’s been a millennia it seems I’ve waited for the long arrival of StS on mobile. After putting 1000+ hours into the PC version, I’m looking forward to starting from scratch and building back up to the legacy I formed on the other console. 

Amazing game, huge replayability, and beautiful designs & balance. A must have for anyone interested in the roguelike-card strategy genre.

reviews.title: Addicted
reviews.text: I am addicted to this game.  My only wish is that once you beat a level, you shouldn’t have to keep starting there over and over again.  I’ve beaten level 1 &2 a bunch of times but can’t beat 3. I have to keep starting at 1 and working my way up again. It gets kinda old after awhile. Can you please change this!

reviews.title: The update ruined the game
reviews.text: I don’t know how In the world this is supposed to be an improvement. The touch controls are unresponsive now and makes the game unpleasantly tedious to play. They were fine before why change it to THIS? Otherwise the game is awesome so I give it 4 stars for now because it’s a port of an amazing game. However please for the love of all that is good please revert this last update!

reviews.title: Solid Port
reviews.text:
It’s Slay the Spire. It’s great. Buy it.

That said, a few things that would be really good to do in order to make the mobile experience top-notch:

- When selecting cards, pop the entire card above where the touch is happening, so you can read the text. 
- Maybe offer a slightly higher framerate option, for those of us willing to sacrifice some battery. Alternatively, it might be a better experience to eliminate some animations entirely but do the ones that stay in at higher framerates. I, for one, would be good with eliminating the “standing” and “arrow” animations but getting butter-smooth card impacts.
- Platform integration: iCloud saves, GameCenter Achievements, alternative music, etc.

Still, it’s Slay the Spire. On mobile. I’m hooked, again.

reviews.title: Super addicting
reviews.text: I don’t usually get in to rogue-likes, but this game has me hooked. I gave it a chance on the PC a couple years ago, but I hardly ever play PC games, so it took a back seat. Decided to pick it up when I saw it on iOS. Glad I did, I can’t put it down. The card mechanics, and the challenge of making it to the end makes me want to keep trying one more time.

reviews.title: Great game, bad port
reviews.text:
So glad this is finally on iOS. But the port ...

The UI around selecting, inspecting and playing cards in combat is pretty awful. It’s difficult to read the card you’re trying to play, both because the text is so small, and because half the card is usually off-screen when you try to select it. It’s also difficult to select a specific card from your hand when you have more than five or so. 

The game plays slower than on other platforms, the text is small and difficult to read, there’s no cloud save, and the game doesn’t support background audio. 

I will play it to death regardless, but I really hope this isn’t the final version. This has potential to be the best version of the game, but iOS presently feels like the worst place to play it.

reviews.title: Ui is wonky
reviews.text:
Own this game on every platform. An amazing game and I have over 700+ hours on it. 
This port needs better card selection UI. The buggy card being stuck in foreground when trying to select a different card is pretty annoying. Trying to read a card but the card keeps showing only 3/4 of the text. 
It would be great if these could be resolved!

reviews.title: Needs internet connection
reviews.text: Slay the Spire should be the perfect game to play offline, but the app doesn’t start up properly without an internet connection. I’ve tried a few times to play this on a train or a plane, and the app just hangs with “Syncing data…” flashing in the corner. It also doesn’t store the sound preferences locally, so the game I expect to be silent starts blasting music on the plane or train while it’s failing to sync. The people who adapted this for iOS really needed to hire a UX designer to help them think through these mobile use cases.

reviews.title: Support Paid Games
reviews.text: I’m not sure why everyone is complaining about the port. Everything works fine. This is a quality game, it’s up there with Dead Cells and Stardew Valley. Games like this should be supported. All the miserable microtransaction free to play not free to play games need to die. Gaming on the iPhone is a market that could be so much better.

reviews.title: Needs optimization for phone
reviews.text:
Good game, simple gameplay with solid mechanics.  Big issue is that it needs optimization.  

Touch controls for cards is very strange and will randomly discard a card or entire hand.  Text (and icons) should still be bigger even with ‘big text’ option.  When highlighting a card, it needs to be raised more especially on iOS due to home bar being in way.  

For the price it’s a great game, it just needs an update to optimize it for phones.

reviews.title: Ui adjustments needed!
reviews.text: Only thing that makes this not 100% awesomeness is simply that the cards don’t display full text properly, it makes it a bit of a pain to sit and try to see the card text. Especially on an iPhone screen, I’ve been confused about card properties and miss fired card plays quite a bit...... other than that I’m super duper happy having this in my hands to pass some time!!!

reviews.title: Great game, controls need work
reviews.text: At the start of my turn a card is pulled up to the middle of my screen and tapping on anything but the bottom left corner of the screen will play it. This is extremely frustrating when trying to read other things on the screen and forgetting that the card is going to get pulled up. Please fix.

reviews.title: Great on PC Horrible mobile controls
reviews.text:
Can’t give the game a proper rating when the very basics don’t work correctly. In a game where one wrong move costs the round is extremely frustrating to try and get the game to work properly. 

Card descriptions are halfway hidden, you click or hold the card to view it fully however sometimes the game selects a card like this automatically. If you tap anywhere on the screen other than your “hand” with all your cards it will cast the card. 

Especially awful when you get large hands with  many cards as you can’t select the right one to cast much less read the right one. 

I hope they figure something out because it’s a great game if it functions. As of now it’s just frustrating worrying about if I can select the right cards, especially later in the game when things get crazy in hand size/multiple abilities.

reviews.title: HUGE BUG!!!!!!! But I love this game
reviews.text: I love this game. However, there is a huge bug where even though I should have unlocked all cards, I am still missing 3 on ironclad. There is no way for me to ever get these cards on my account as I have completed all unlocks. I looked this issue up and others have said the same.

reviews.title: Amazing game, UI just needs a little more work
reviews.text:
As many others have said, this is a brilliant game that’s absolutely perfect for mobile play — it just has a few UI annoyances, mainly when trying to preview cards in your hand or potions and relics. 

If the devs can optimize the UI better for small screens, it’ll be an easy 5/5. Until then, I still highly recommend it, just be aware the UI isn’t perfect yet.

reviews.title: Can’t switch to beta art due to touch controls
reviews.text: Love the game but it’s a real bummer to complete the spire with a character and unlock the beta art for cards, only to not be able to switch them out. Tried many times using different methods and adjusting/rotating the screen, but no matter what I do when I try to select the box for the beta artwork it exits the screen back to the card menu.

reviews.title: Best on PC
reviews.text: I love this game. I have almost 500 hours on steam, and I’ve been anxiously awaiting its release on mobile. Like many others have already mentioned, I would like to see the game altered to be more compatible with a small phone screen and backup across devices is a must. Additionally, the game is a HUGE drain on battery. I knew it would be bad, but the game even crashes on startup if my phone is in battery saver mode. If these issues get fixed, it’s an easy 5 star review.

reviews.title: Great Game that loses so much on mobile
reviews.text:
The game is just so impossible to see on the phone and there are absolutely no setting to adjust anything to be bigger, not to mention that the controls are god awful. Never have I played a game where the same button to read the cards information can also automatically play the card, there needs to be some delineation 

This is a deck building card game, I need to be able to see it. 

 Honestly I would prefer a refund and would advise anyone to NOT BUY THIS the console version is 5 stars. This is 2 because the mechanics of the game that are interesting are impossible to see or play without straining your eyes 

 Otherwise fun and engaging on console where I first played it first, decided to buy it for the phone which was my mistake.

reviews.title: Great game but phone can be buggy
reviews.text: I love the is game, I have it on steam so I hate to complain but it’s a pretty bad bug where my ascensions aren’t being registered. You’re supposed to unlock the next ascension even when you lose the heart, but three times it never went through and I had to repeat the ascension. Please, for the love of god fix this

reviews.title: Love the game. Hate the app.
reviews.text:
I play this on PC all the time, and loved it enough to buy it again on my phone. That being said, this port is terrible. It’s the exact same UI but shrunk down to a phone screen, making it really awkward to interact with. This version also seems to be riddled with bugs too. In a single run, I’ve had it randomly skip my turn 3 times, use cards on its own several times, and use the wrong card multiple times as well.

TL;DR: stay away from this port until devs decide to put any effort into it

reviews.title: Great game. Serious bug
reviews.text: An amazing game I have no trouble recommending, but with a serious flaw. The iOS port cuts off some of the card text. When you play, you cannot see what your cards do. Selecting the card to individually see what they are is tedious, and risks accidentally playing them. It’s a noticeable scuff on an otherwise flawless gem. Please fix

reviews.title: Gameplay is great, UI is awful
reviews.text:
This game is addicting, but the port seems pretty lazy. If you’re looking to get this game, I’d recommend the console version instead. 

On an iPhone X:

Text is way too small, but if you change it to larger text in settings then everything overlaps weird. 

Not touch friendly. Buttons/click areas are tiny. 

The bottom of your hand is cut off. You have to drag the card up to see the text and that sometimes results in accidental casting. 

If you select a card, touching another part of the screen won’t always cancel the cast, which also results in accidental casting. 

When dragging cards up, it sometimes results in closing the app because the iphone registers it as a gesture to close since the hand is so close to the edge.

reviews.title: WHY NO CLOUD SAVE??! :(
reviews.text: Great game but lost all my save data when I deleted the game for a bit. Figured it would all be backed up to the cloud because it was constantly “Syncing data…” but I was wrong, extremely disappointed and shocked when I redownloaded the game a bit later. Please fix this to be up to date with modern capabilities. Otherwise great game.

reviews.title: DO NOT UNINSTALL
reviews.text:
Fun little game…however…it should be noted (perhaps upon game purchase) that uninstalling will wipe out all your info, save files, progress, etc….EVERYTHING!
Game was running poorly so I did an uninstall/reinstall, thinking it would take care of the bugginess. I guess, in a way, it did help…just not in a preferable way. 
Even though I’ll most likely enjoy starting over, this should’ve been mentioned in the Game Details 🫤

reviews.title: I’m so addicted
reviews.text: Love this game through and through. I am used to playing it on controller though and have had several instances where I will sometimes accidentally play cards without meaning to with touch controls. Not a big deal, but controller support on iOS would be a game changer for me!

reviews.title: Solid port and quality game
